# v2.91-dev

Security hardening release, continuing the review that produced v2.88-dev and
v2.89-dev. This one strengthens **restore** — the single most powerful operation
in the app, since it can replace the entire dataset, user accounts included.

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes below say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

## Hardened

- **Restoring a backup now asks you to confirm it's really you.** Both the
  upload restore and the "restore a saved backup" flow now require you to
  re-enter your **own account password** — and a current MFA code if your
  account uses MFA — before the restore runs. Being signed in is no longer
  enough on its own, so a restore can't be triggered by a session that isn't
  actively confirmed by the person at the keyboard.

- **A backup that carries user accounts is only accepted when it's encrypted.**
  User credentials are only ever written into an encrypted backup. An
  unencrypted file that nonetheless claims to include accounts is therefore
  corrupt or was altered, and the restore now refuses it outright rather than
  trusting the account data inside. Ordinary backups — encrypted standard
  backups, passphrase-protected portable backups, and credential-free backups —
  restore exactly as before.

- **Uploaded backups have a size limit.** An uploaded archive is now capped
  (512 MB by default) before it is read into memory, so an oversized or
  malformed upload can't exhaust the server. The limit can be raised with the
  new optional `BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB` setting if you have an unusually large
  dataset.

## Upgrading

No database changes; the update applies automatically.

- The password (and MFA) prompt appears automatically in the restore dialog —
  nothing to configure. Keep your own account credentials to hand when
  restoring.
- `BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB` is optional and documented in `.env.example`; the
  default is fine for typical installs.

The restore changes are reflected in the README and the in-app help
(**Backup & Restore**).
